I just watched Michigan’s offensive film vs Indiana. Can’t believe I did this for free, I need a beer. The video is linked below. These were my takeaways:

1. Bryant Haines is the best defensive coordinator in the history of the sport... EVER! He dominated Michigan with a mediocre at best DL. None of those guys start at other contending schools, and for the most part none of those guys are winning true 1v1s with OL, but they execute twist in the run and pass game at a high level, and Bryant Haines guesses right on those calls seemingly...ALWAYS?!

​2. Jason Beck did SOME good stuff and made SOME good adjustments that I point out, but they were few and far between, but they all felt like one-offs that couldn't be done twice. He made a few egregious calls, (the last play of the game running switch verts is worse than boot on the goal line!!!) but for the most part... Haines is just better at his job, and it ain't close. Levels.

​3. Since coming back from injury, Manuel Beigel has been unplayable. He's clueless where to go on combos and has abysmal technique on down blocks. I also point out a couple of times where the rhino being no threat hurts Michigan's pass concepts.

​4. Outside zone is a good play for Michigan because they are good at it.... it created both RB explosives vs PSU... but you need to run it out of different looks. Michigan tried to repeatedly run it how OSU did against them well last week... they clearly made adjustments and we didn't care and just kept calling it.

5. ​Outside of Manuel Beigel, Oline runs duo very well and I thought it was the best play to run vs Indiana's twisting. They got away from it for some reason. Counter is HORRIBLE vs those twists. I now understand why OSU didn't run any in that tape.

6. ​Per usual, the "bad jet sweep" was just poor blocking and a missed assignment on the perimeter. Debatable read by Tommy Carr. At the same time - Michigan clearly sucks at these plays AND they're getting easily schemed up because the personnel and formations are so predictable. Probably cut that out.

​7. Any time Indiana got into man, Michigan didn't get open. If I were them, I would have stayed in it all day. Marsh becomes really the only threat outside of well-designed 1-read plays.

8. ​Tommy Carr was majorly gun shy after the interception. A lot of times I thought the ball should have been out and it just wasn't. He didn't run boot well, seemingly afraid to throw the first read. I was harsh on Tommy in this video, but a lot of this stuff is so easily fixable, and he was facing the literal best in the sport. I'll explain why this is poorly done and doesn't support the title (help from supporting cast).

1. If you agree sacks are a QB stat, then so are pressures. Having a low pressure rate because you routinely get the ball out quickly doesn't imply your protection is great.

2. Separation is a junk stat. It might be useful information if dug into deeper, but presented as an average yardage figure, it gives us nothing useful to say about QBs or even their supporting cast. 
 To say nothing of a QB who can create separation by throwing on the move and using their eyes and pump fakes to create even more separation for the receiver they decide to throw to.

3. Drop % - Too basic; drops aren't created equally. An offense with twice as many drops can still be less harmful than an offense where most of the drops are on deep balls and 3rd/4th downs that would have extended drives. A lot of drops on screens, early downs, and would be failed completions on 3rd and long simply don't hurt the QB as much.

4. YAC - Too basic; YAC isn't created equally. Need some kind of expected YAC component so you're not just dinging a QB for the style of offense he's in. If you throw more screens and passes behind the LOS and check downs, you're going to end up with more YAC because of where the ball is being caught. That doesn't mean a 3-yard gain with 11 YAC on a 3rd-and-15 is a good play. For that matter an 8-yard pass with no YAC on 3rd-and-15 usually isn't a good play either.

I'm not saying he did basic bitch work because he's a Patriots fan. I'd say these exact same things if he was a fan of any team.

These things as they were used do not actually tell us anything about the QB's supporting cast, nor do they do enough to separate the QB's performance from making these numbers what they are.
